detail.abstract: A trader deciding where to post a limit order knows three things for free: which side they intend to quote, how far from mid, and how long they are willing to wait. Whether limit order book (LOB) microstructure adds anything beyond those three choices is an empirical question, and one rarely posed against a baseline simple enough to make the answer interpretable. We pose it directly. Using 269,330 LOB snapshots collected over a 70.5-day calendar window from Kraken across BTC/USD, ETH/USD and SOL/USD, we predict whether the opposite best quote reaches or crosses a limit price posted at a given distance from mid, within a fixed horizon, and we benchmark against a 16-cell lookup table containing only the mean historical crossing rate for each combination of quote offset, horizon and side. That table is a demanding reference: both conditioning variables carry large monotone effects on the crossing rate, spanning 0.46 across offsets on BTC/USD at 300 s and comparable ranges elsewhere (Table 2). Microstructure features beat it, modestly and consistently. Under a snapshot-grouped temporal split with a 990-second embargo, gradient-boosted trees over 63 microstructure features gain +0.048 and +0.060 AUC on BTC and ETH (Table 3 reports all figures to four decimals). Under a blocked split constructed so that training and test partitions span overlapping price regimes, the gain is positive on all three assets. Rotating the arbitrary block phase gives ten phase assignments with disjoint test sets per asset, and all thirty are positive: means of +0.047, +0.038 and +0.035, with no rotation below +0.013. Across-phase standard deviations are 0.0052, 0.0144 and 0.0103. The split scheme matters, and revealed something we would otherwise have misreported. Under the temporal split, training and test partitions occupied almost disjoint price ranges: overlap of 0.129, 0.073 and 0.251. SOL/USD appeared to show a negative microstructure effect there, which reversed to +0.027 once the partitions spanned comparable price regimes. We report both schemes throughout, since neither substitutes for the other: the temporal split respects forecasting order, and the blocked split reduces temporal distribution shift between partitions. We also compare model classes, holding the input representation fixed. Gradient-boosted trees lead an LSTM on BTC and ETH under both representations, but on SOL/USD the ordering flips with representation: trees lead by 0.0013 on 109 features and trail by 0.0475 on the 63-feature microstructure subset. We draw no general ordering. An earlier version claimed model class was decisive; that rested on a defective survival head. 1 Finally, we document five defects in our own pipeline, each of which produced plausible, publishable-looking numbers, and the specific checks that caught them. We consider this the most transferable part of the work.

detail.abstract: Online advertising is a central marketing lever for e-commerce retailers, yet it complicates operational planning by simultaneously stimulating product demand and increasing product returns. Motivated by the practice of a fashion retailer on Amazon, we study a retailer's joint inventory and advertising problem across multiple products over a single season, in which advertising has both direct and cross-product spillover effects on demand and returns. Using linear net-demand and return models that capture both effects, we formulate a contextual stochastic optimization model that jointly determines inventory levels and advertising decisions before the selling season. Because ad clicks are realized only after the advertising decision, the predictive covariates are partially observable and decision-dependent, and their joint distribution with the demand and return errors is unknown. We therefore develop an estimate-then-robustify (ETR) approach grounded in a data-driven robust satisficing framework. We establish a finite-sample guarantee on the out-ofsample profit of the ETR solution that holds for any parameter estimator, show that the solution is asymptotically optimal when the estimator is consistent and the profit target approaches the empirical optimal profit, and derive a mixed-integer conic approximation via affine recourse adaptation that is exact for a single product. On the retailer's data, ETR improves out-of-sample profit over conventional estimate-then-optimize by 6.39% and earns the higher profit in 74.5% of instances, with the largest gains when training data are scarce; the gain falls to 1.02% when the decision model omits cross-product spillovers.

detail.abstract: This paper presents an institutional and financial blueprint to resolve the chronic economic duality and low-productivity traps that exclude micro and small enterprises (MSEs) in Peru from the modern economy. Drawing on New Institutional Economics (NIE) and structured finance principles, we diagnose why legacy state-led interventions (e.g., PRONAA, Qali Warma, Compras a MYPErú) and simplified tax regimes (e.g., RUS) systematically fail. These frameworks focus on administrative compliance or untranched liquidity matching while leaving process asymmetries, high transaction cost thresholds (τ cost), and short cognitive time horizons unaltered, forcing producers into technological and labor precarization loops to survive. To break this deadlock, we propose a two-phase operational model. Phase 1 establishes an Operational Incubation Sieve governed by a non-aligned, decentralized technical triumvirate recruited from elite universities (UNALM, UNI, UP, PUCP, UNMSM). This framework shifts the development paradigm by separating operational roles, training entrepreneurs strictly as world-class Production Sub-Managers while transferring financial and legal execution to a centralized Management Upgrade. By leveraging institutional brand equity under an asymmetric asset forfeiture model, the academic boards provide a credible, uncompromised quality signal and a compiled performance ledger (the "Reputational Passport") to the market. Phase 2 activates a bankruptcy-remote, pay-through Revolving Master Trust Fund to bypass commercial banking monopolies entirely. Rather than underwriting individual borrower credit debt-as seen in the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) pass-through model-the trust securitizes the verified, real-economy trade receivables of Phase 1 Alumni operating as corporate subcontractors. The revolving structure operates as a structural maturity matchmaker, coupling high-velocity, short-term micro-receivables from the multi-decade duration locks required by institutional fixed-income and social-impact investors. Finally, we implement self-executing legal safeguards-including irrevocable step-in rights, fast-track technical arbitration panels, and geofenced SUNARP joint liability registrations-to strip informal intermediaries of the "good faith buyer" defense and eliminate contract cheating (ruleteo). This comprehensive framework demonstrates how micro-scale efficiency can organically fund labor formalization, shifting public policy from poverty mitigation to structural economic transformation.

detail.abstract: Quantum computing has attracted about $15 billion of investor capital and $41 billion of confirmed government funding, while the listed pure-play companies have reported under $1 billion of revenue since 2021. This working paper asks what fault-tolerant quantum computers will be able to sell once they work as promised, and whether that can pay for them. The method is Fermi estimation, with every input cited, every equation shown, every estimate bounded, and each conclusion tested at the end of each range most favourable to quantum computing. Of ten algorithms that dominate the literature, only two keep a decisive advantage over GPUs and AI once error correction is counted: breaking encryption, which has no lawful commercial buyer, and exact simulation of strongly correlated molecules beyond about 25-30 orbitals. That market is about $100 million a year of today's simulation budgets and at most $2-10 billion a year to vendors in the late 2030s, enough to keep perhaps 0.2-20 machines busy, against about $100-150 billion to reach fault tolerance by 2032. Governments, for security, are the realistic buyer. Thirteen counter-arguments are tested; one, a new algorithm with a broad exponential speed-up, could overturn the result. The purpose is public economics: putting the tools to judge a technology of public importance, paid for partly with public money, in the hands of the public. The model code is open (MIT) at github.com/desfitz/quantum-limits, and the paper, deck and code are archived at doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24150083. Companion paper: The Macroeconomic Limits of AI Compute (SSRN 7620359). Not investment advice.

detail.abstract: Autonomous AI analysts can run hundreds of specifications in minutes and report the most striking, and recent studies show that they can be steered into specification search and that their conclusions track the priors they are given. We ask what an independent referee can promise about the findings of an analyst whose behaviour it cannot model. We propose the rolling seal: data are split into an open exploration set and sealed folds; the analyst explores freely and commits claims, each of whose required evidence is fixed at commit by e-LOND; at the end of each episode one fresh fold is opened once, each open claim's betting e-value on it multiplies into the claim's running evidence, and the spent fold is released to the analyst. We prove that the false discovery rate over certified claims is at most 𝛼 for every analyst, every ordering and revision of claims and every dependence between them, that the guarantee rests on sealing rather than logging, and that commit-time choices by a language model, such as grouping tests into hypothesis families, cannot weaken it. We give exact nonparametric e-values for differences and levels of bounded means, with starting bets from the exploration data, and describe HERDSMAN, an open-source referee with an encrypted vault, a hash-chained ledger, signed certificates and a Model Context Protocol interface for agents. In 1,500 simulated studies, unrefereed reports contained false findings in 93% to 100% of null studies while the rolling seal's false discovery rate never exceeded 1.0%; a re-used holdout that released per-claim estimates certified a composite claim built from noise in 100% of null studies, the rolling seal in 0%. Validity costs power, which we quantify. In a live case study, six instances of a frontier AI agent analysed a synthetic lending experiment under neutral, pressured, sceptical and segment-hunting briefs. Their unrefereed reports contained no false effects; every claim they then committed was true, and the referee certified 81 of the 101, leaving mainly small arrears effects unconfirmed.

detail.abstract: This article critically examines the development of bio-based thermoplastic elastomers (TPEs) for sustainable rubber manufacturing, focusing on renewable feedstocks, dynamic vulcanization, phase morphology, interfacial compatibilization, mechanical and thermal performance, reprocessing, and industrial adoption. A structured narrative review was developed from the 15 references supplied for the study, supplemented by targeted checks of publisher and scholarly records and selected recent literature. The evidence indicates that biobased TPEs can be produced by combining renewable thermoplastic matrices, particularly polylactide (PLA), with natural rubber, epoxidized natural rubber, or bio-derived elastomeric components. Dynamic vulcanization and in-situ compatibilization can generate fine or cocontinuous morphologies and improve toughness relative to brittle neat PLA in specific formulations. However, laboratory performance does not establish commercial readiness. Variability in natural feedstocks, moisture sensitivity, thermal-processing windows, cure control, cost, scale-up, durability, and end-of-life infrastructure remain important barriers. The review concludes that bio-based TPE development should be evaluated through a coupled framework linking feedstock origin, polymer chemistry, processing, morphology, service performance, and life-cycle outcomes. Because this is a literature synthesis, it reports no new experimental measurements or pooled statistical estimates.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether Tanzania’s persistent current account deficit reflects structural economic weakness or investment-driven economic growth. Using a descriptive analysis of secondary data from the Bank of Tanzania and international financial institutions, the study evaluates trends in Tanzania’s current account balance and the composition of imports across six selected financial years between 2000/2001 and 2023/2024. The findings reveal that Tanzania consistently recorded current account deficits, increasing from USD 535.0 million in 2000/2001 to USD 2,767.4 million in 2023/2024, with fluctuations throughout the period. Import composition analysis indicates that capital and intermediate goods constitute major components of Tanzania’s import expenditure, reflecting substantial investments in infrastructure, industrialization, and productive capacity. In 2023/2024, capital goods imports reached USD 5,580.3 million, while intermediate goods amounted to USD 4,519.5 million, exceeding consumer goods imports of USD 3,683.3 million. These findings suggest that Tanzania’s current account deficit is largely associated with investment-related imports rather than excessive consumption. The paper concludes that Tanzania’s current account deficit can be interpreted as a reflection of economic transformation and long-term growth ambitions rather than solely a sign of economic weakness. Nevertheless, the sustainability of such deficits depends on the productive utilization of imported capital, effective external financing, and the country's capacity to generate future export earnings.

detail.abstract: Before the 2026 midterm elections we published win probabilities for every House seat, Senate race and governorship, first six days before the vote and again on its eve, with the rule we would use to score them. AP has now called 493 of the 506 races. The most accurate forecast we published came from the betting markets, averaged across exchanges. Our headline forecast weighted markets and polls equally. It called two more races correctly but was slightly less accurate across all races, because the polls and the markets erred in the same places and averaging mainly added the polls' larger errors. The markets were also more accurate than every major rating organisation. All forecasters, ourselves included, missed in the same direction. Democrats won the national House vote by about 13.6 points, some five points more than markets or polls expected, and our methods, which filtered out the disagreements between exchanges and between pollsters, could not detect an error that both shared. We close with rules for 2028.

detail.abstract: This study examines the convergence of the per capita biomass material footprint across 111 countries over 1970-2021 and its long-run determinants. We first apply the Phillips and Sul (2007, 2009) club convergence method to test whether countries follow a single global path or split into clubs. We then examine the relationships between the biomass material footprint and per capita GDP, the fossil fuel footprint, arable land, cereal yield and the animal protein share of the food supply with panel Fourier Toda-Yamamoto causality and cointegration tests. Long-run coefficients are estimated with mean group estimators that allow for heterogeneous slopes (CCE-MG, AMG, FCCE-MG) and with the cross-sectionally augmented ARDL (CS-ARDL) estimator. The countries do not converge to a single steady state but form six clubs. Per capita income, fossil fuel material use and cereal yield raise the biomass footprint in the long run in the full sample and the largest club; in the full sample, arable land works in the same direction and the income elasticity stays below one. Cereal yield and fossil fuel use dominate in the second club, and arable land in the third. Although the animal protein share is linked to the footprint through causality and cointegration, it has no long-run effect once income and production-side factors are controlled for. The main findings are robust to the choice of estimator and to dropping this variable. Resource efficiency policies should therefore be differentiated by the production structure of each club, and supply-side efficiency gains should be paired with demand-side measures.

detail.abstract: Legal systems increasingly accept that organisations can injure the people who work in them, but they do so through vocabularies of risk, injury and harassment that fit poorly the phenomenon psychologists call organizational dehumanization: the experience of being treated as an instrument, an interchangeable unit denied individuality and voice. This article asks how far four legal systems (Germany, England and Wales, France and Brazil) can name and address that experience when it arises from the ordinary design of procedure rather than from an identifiable act or an avowed policy of mistreatment. Using doctrinal and comparative analysis, supplemented by an interpretive reading of the Brazilian novel O Prédio que Aprendeu a Escutar as a work of institutional criticism (used as an interpretive case, not as evidence), the article advances a central thesis. The legal concept closest to mechanistic dehumanization, the prohibition on treating a person as a mere object, operates at the scale of acts, whereas organizational dehumanization operates at the scale of arrangements; and monitoring systems that record outcomes (absence, diagnosis, complaint) tend not to register arrangement-scale suffering at all. In the sources examined, regulatory risk-assessment duties (the German Arbeitsschutzgesetz and Brazil's revised NR-1) are the only vehicles that reach arrangements without proof of fault or intent, but their vocabulary has no explicit place for treatment-type factors, while French criminal law reaches arrangements only through proven deliberate policy. The article tests the thesis against the strongest objection, the Weberian defence of impersonality, identifies conditions that would falsify it, and proposes three modest interpretive and procedural consequences. The contribution is an analytical distinction and a comparative synthesis; it is not an empirical finding. The author critically reviewed, edited, verified, and assumed responsibility for all legal analysis, argumentation, sources, interpretations, data, and conclusions contained in the final manuscript.

detail.title: The Prize Paradox: Value–Cost Coupling in Coercive Acquisition

detail.abstract: Where a prize's value depends on people, networks or trust that coercion disrupts, its value to the acquirer falls and the cost of taking it rises as more force is applied. Beyond some level of force the acquirer can expect to pay more than it gains. We call this the Prize Paradox. How strongly it binds depends on coupling, which has three parts: operational complexity, network embeddedness and identity salience. Value and cost change in steps rather than smoothly, at events to which firms and governments respond. Some of what is lost at those steps cannot be recovered by reducing force once the step has been reached. Acquirers tend to overestimate the prize and underestimate the cost, and the cost error is largest at the first threshold beyond any at which third parties have acted before. As coupling rises, a rational acquirer that values what the prize produces should choose less force. Heavy force against such a prize should therefore be uncommon, and where it occurs it should come with an aim other than the prize's output or with prewar estimates that proved too optimistic. The paper offers a framework with one measured case and one forecast, not a statistical test. Four historical cases show variation in coupling consistent with it, and a fifth, Hong Kong, illustrates the limit of its scope. Russia's attempt on Ukraine is the one case that can be followed through several thresholds with public data, and the one case of heavy force against a coupled political prize. Among the assets Russia took under the same force, what each kept follows its coupling: occupied farmland went on producing grain, while the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, taken intact, has produced no power for the grid since 2022. Ukrainian opinion of Russia fell sharply at the seizure of Crimea in 2014. Europe's purchases of Russian gas did not change through eight years of conflict, and the largest withdrawals by third parties, of reserves, banking access and oil buyers, came only at the 2022 invasion. The forecast is for Chinese coercion of Taiwan and its chip industry. From recent shipping crises and crisis exercises, we expect companies to pull back first, at a declared quarantine, with orders for older chips moving before leading-edge orders, and governments to impose their costliest measures later, at a blockade, led by the United States and Japan. The claims concern direction and order, not size.

detail.abstract: Deterministic cashflow projections as function of market probability are compared to the probability distribution from Monte-Carlo runs to examine the effect of extraction of surplus capital. Results are consistent for annual extraction of surplus above a limit of 115% German HGBdiscounted liabilities or higher. Pension safety depends mainly on initial funding and asset allocation and can then be modelled deterministically. For the investor it is preferable to extract earlier if the required rate of return, used to discount extractions, approaches 10% and if repeat investments are possible even at zero discount rate. At typical funding above 90% HGB there is less than 0.1% probability that capital runs out before year 20, at 80% HGB around year 15. These numbers apply to typical long-term asset allocations and pension liabilities.

title: Toward a Unified Account of Singular Causal Explanation under Uncertainty

detail.title: Toward a Unified Account of Singular Causal Explanation under Uncertainty

detail.abstract:
Explanation is a fundamental facet of human cognition relating both to how we make sense of the world and to how we assign and communicate credit. Typically these aspects have been studied separately. This thesis takes a step toward unifying them by developing a modelling framework for understanding how people generate explanations in uncertain situations.

In Chapter 1, I introduce tools for understanding explanation including causal model theory and structural causal models. Chapters 2-4 describe a series of three behavioural experiments and computational analyses that show causal inference and causal selection combine in shaping causal explanations.

Chapter 2 reports Experiment 1 (N=215) examining judgements about simple scenarios in which causal relationships and parameters are provided. I use information gain to tease out the relative contribution of the products of inference. By comparing a suite of computational models, I show that participants engage in both inference and selection. I also find participants favour explanations that highlight causes that depend on these inferences over those that do not. 

In Chapters 3 and 4, I apply the combined modelling approach developed in Chapter 2 to a more complex situation: a rich gridworld environment instead of simple scenarios, and free text explanations instead of forced choice. In Chapter 3, I obtain the causal strengths governing the gridworld from a set of participants (N=90). In Chapter 4, a new set of participants (N=255) see subsets of causes and outcomes, and give explanations in natural language for what they see. I model their responses with my combined inference and selection model, and find that people are rarely lost for words, giving coherent explanations that correspond to given variables when the outcome is expected, and imputing latent factors when it isn't.

Overall, the thesis demonstrates that human explanatory behaviour in uncertain and naturalistic settings can be captured with a unified model that incorporates both inference and selection.

detail.abstract: Participants in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) display a cyclical spending pattern, with food expenditure peaking immediately after monthly benefit receipt. Yet it remains unclear how participants respond when benefits arrive earlier than expected. We exploit changes in the benefit disbursement schedule during the 2018-2019 government shutdown, which shifted February 2019 benefits into January, along with subsequent state-level adjustments in March and April, to study how early and unexpected disbursements affect food shopping behavior among program participants. Drawing on NielsenIQ consumer panel data and a triple difference design, we show that the early disbursement of benefits led to a 6% reduction in February food spending among SNAP-eligible households. This reduction was driven primarily by larger proportional cuts in healthier food and fruit and vegetable purchases, although we find no statistically significant effect on overall diet quality. These effects were concentrated in states that issue benefits within the first week of the calendar month. We also show that households did not exhibit the typical post-disbursement spending spike following the early February benefit disbursement; rather, the shorter interval between successive benefit payments helped smooth within-month expenditures and temporarily flatten the SNAP cycle. Finally, subsequent state-level schedule adjustments in March and April helped mitigate what would otherwise have been a sharp depletion in food expenditure during those months. We discuss policy implications related to benefit timing and adequacy during major program disruptions.

detail.abstract: Prescription drug prices are determined through a chain of interactions among manufacturers, insurers, and consumers. A regulator seeking to lower drug prices must choose which point in the chain to regulate and which drugs to target. How are the effects of drug price regulations distributed among market participants, and how does that guide a regulator's preferred choices? We develop a model of a drug market with rebate bargaining and community-rated premiums. A net price ceiling transfers surplus from manufacturers to insurers, and a copay cap reaches drug users directly with insurers and manufacturers splitting the cost. Beyond that, consumers may be affected through premiums, which only move when drug users are marginal enrollees. A consumer-welfare-maximizing regulator should cap copays, while a spending-minimizing regulator can use either instrument. Copay caps should target drugs with high out-of-pocket prices, many users, and elastic utilization; net price ceilings should target high net spending. Applied to insulin in Medicare Part D, the model implies that Medicare's $35 insulin copay cap raises fills by 3% at a cost borne by insurers and manufacturers rather than by other consumers.

detail.abstract: Gross domestic product (GDP) counts a meal cooked in a restaurant and a child minded in a nursery, but not the same meal cooked or the same child cared for by a mother at home. This paper examines that exclusion. It reviews the conceptual basis of the production boundary in the System of National Accounts (SNA), the methods used to value unpaid care, and the range of published estimates, and it uses India as a case study. Valuations of unpaid household and care work range from about 9 per cent of global GDP on a minimum-wage basis to more than 60 per cent of national GDP under a full output approach, and women supply roughly three quarters of the hours. The paper argues that the gap is not a rounding error but a structural bias: GDP overstates growth when care moves from home to market, hides the cost of withdrawing mothers from paid work, and leaves the largest input into human capital formation unpriced. It concludes that unpaid care should not be folded into headline GDP, but that regular household satellite accounts, as now recommended by the 2025 SNA, should be treated as core economic statistics and used in fiscal, labour and social policy.

detail.abstract: Adam Smith's Theory of Moral Sentiments (1759; hereafter ToMS) explains moral sentiments in terms of their social function. We ask whether this anticipates Darwin's account of group selection in The Descent of Man (1871), in which instincts that offer no direct survival advantage to individuals (e.g., altruism) may still spread because tribes rich in them prevail. Through close reading and a concordance of Smith's many attributions of design to Nature, we present four pieces of evidence, ranging from Smith's grounding of moral judgment in instinct to his distinction between efficient and final causes. We argue that Smith anticipates the structure of Darwin's explanation, but not its mechanism. Smith anticipates the problem group selection addresses-a sentiment that indirectly benefits the group-but not group selection itself. For instance, for a sentiment such as remorse, Smith and Darwin would agree on what it leads a person to do and what it is for, but differ on its origin.

detail.abstract: The long-standing pathologies of Public Administration, such as bureaucracy, are often attributed to abstract causes like a "bad mentality". This article argues that game theory offers a much stronger analytical tool, interpreting dysfunctions as the rational consequences of a "game" with distorted incentives. Through a systematic review of international literature, we propose an original, coherent framework of interventions called the "Game Architecture Framework". This model provides the reformer-"designer" with five strategic levers, namely changing the rules, altering payoffs, increasing transparency, enhancing repetition, and introducing trusted third parties. Its practical value is demonstrated through indicative applications in the Greek Public Administration. Furthermore, the framework is placed in dialogue with established, state-of-the-art reform movements, highlighting its distinct diagnostic superiority. The central conclusion is that the true challenge for reform is not writing new laws, but redesigning the game so that collectively beneficial behavior also becomes individually rational.

detail.abstract:
Information-driven sampling schemes-most notably Dollar Imbalance Bars (DIB) introduced by López de Prado (2018)-seek to subordinate chronological wall-clock time to the arrival rate of informed directional order flow, thereby recovering partial asymptotic normality and variance stationarity in high-frequency financial return series. Yet deploying textbook DIB formulations on live electronic limit order books exposes two severe mathematical pathologies that have remained unaddressed in the econometrics literature: (i) Zero-Drift Singularity and Micro-Bar Collapse, wherein balanced two-sided order flow drives the exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) of signed notional flow toward zero (ν i → 0), causing the dynamic threshold θ * k to collapse and triggering bursts of degenerate single-tick bars dominated by discrete bid-ask bounce; and (ii) Coupled Dual-EWMA Absorbing Collapse, wherein simultaneously adapting expected bar cardinality Tk and expected signed drift νi induces a multiplicative positive-feedback contraction loop that locks the sampler into a 1-tick absorbing state. 

       We prove both instability mechanisms from first principles and introduce the Regularized Adaptive Dollar Imbalance Bar (RA-DIB) operator, which anchors the target information horizon E 0 [T ] while imposing a structural prior-scaled drift floor ν min = ηE 0 [d], an absolute minimum threshold bound θ min , a microstructure noise cardinality floor T min , and causal session-boundary resets. Evaluating 70 months of complete tick-by-tick CME Globex MDP 3.0 Top-of-Book and Trade (TBBO) records across six flagship futures contracts (/ES, /NQ, /RTY, /GC, /CL, and /6E; 1.6616 × 10 9 trades, January 2021-October 2026, yielding 8, 000, 323 RA-DIB bars), we demonstrate that RA-DIB eliminates 100% of degenerate micro-bars (T k < 10), compresses return excess kurtosis by 54.5% to 66.7% relative to chronological time bars, reduces normalized Jarque-Bera statistics by 79.3% to 88.9%, and attenuates Engle's ARCH-LM(5) conditional heteroskedasticity R 2 by up to 54.5% while executing deterministically at 64.48 million ticks/second (15.51 ns per trade).

detail.abstract: Poland has sold retail Treasury savings bonds every month since 1999, including bonds that pay consumer price inflation plus a margin fixed on the day of purchase. This paper reports the ex-post nominal and real returns of every series that matured by September 2026: 1,054 series in nine families, from three-month fixed-rate bonds to ten-year inflation-indexed bonds. Cash flows are rebuilt from the official interest rates and issue letters; the 955 amounts rebuilt from the formulas match the interest published by the Ministry of Finance to the grosz, and for 99 older series the published amounts are used directly. Real returns are internal rates of return of cash flows deflated with the official consumer price index, before and after the personal income tax that applied to each series. The median real annual return of the 949 series with a term of at least one year was 1.73% before tax and 0.92% after tax (943 series with after-tax values). Ten-year inflation-indexed bonds (EDO) returned a median of 2.75% a year above inflation before tax and 1.98% after tax, and 137 of 144 EDO series beat inflation after tax. Their real return is closely associated with the margin fixed at purchase, from 3.95% for the 2004 issues (margin 3.5 percentage points) to 0.56% for the 2013 issues (margin 1.5 to 1.75 points). Three-month fixed-rate bonds and the discontinued three-year floating-rate bonds lost to inflation in the median, and so did six-year family bonds after tax. For long bonds the results change little under alternative ways of measuring inflation. All data are open under CC BY 4.0.

detail.abstract: This paper extends the Unified Diwakar's Plate (UDP) framework from single-option visualization to static multi-leg portfolios, including iron condors, butterflies, ratio spreads, and calendars. Fixed concentric strike coordinates and a moving spot-relative ring organize signed portfolio values, intrinsic and extrinsic components, settlement cash flows, and sensitivity information. A boundary-corrected Gaussian kernel maps leg-level Greeks to signed and gross radial attribution fields while preserving their portfolio aggregates under radial integration. Vanna, Charm, Speed, and Volga are formulated under specified differentiation and volatility-shock conventions; the implemented numerical mapping benchmark focuses on Gamma. European Black-Scholes-Merton (BSM) examples verify four initial valuations, an iron-condor intermediate state, terminal-payoff behavior, and Gaussian integration tolerances. Original numerical figures illustrate the distinction between strike-attributed fields and spot-scenario sensitivities. The framework is a model-agnostic representation, not a new pricing theory, empirically validated forecasting method, or trading rule.

detail.abstract: Chinese banks have shifted their deposits toward time deposits. Using quarterly data on 229 banks from 2010 to 2023 and exogenous monetary policy shocks, we show that this shift weakens the transmission of monetary easing to bank lending. Banks with more time deposits cut deposit rates less after easing, because time deposits reprice only at maturity, and attract fewer new demand deposits, which carry most of the liquidity that easing injects. The effect survives a shift-share instrument, concentrates in banks near the loan-to-deposit cap, and extends to firm investment and employment and to aggregate credit and output.

detail.abstract: This paper derives the density function of the product of a Wishart matrix and a normal vector that are independently distributed. Unlike existing results, we allow the covariance matrix of the Wishart distribution and that of the normal vector to differ, and we do not assume them to be proportional. In this general setting, the density is shown to admit a two-dimensional integral representation. We further obtain the density of linear combinations of the product. For a single linear combination, it is again expressed as a two-dimensional integral whose integrand involves the modified Bessel function of the second kind, and the special case in which the covariance matrix of the normal vector is proportional to the inverse of the covariance matrix of the Wishart distribution is treated explicitly. In addition, we show that the characteristic function of any number 𝑝 of linear combinations is a one-dimensional integral, from which the density of 𝑝 < 𝑚 linear combinations is recovered as a (𝑝 + 1)-dimensional integral; together with the two-dimensional representation of the full product, this makes the density of any 𝑝 linear combinations available from an integral of dimension at most min(𝑝 + 1, 𝑚-𝑝 + 2), where 𝑚 is the dimension of the product. All resulting expressions can be evaluated numerically, and their accuracy is illustrated by a comparison with simulation; the product defines a new family of matrix-variate mean-variance mixtures of multivariate normal distributions.

detail.abstract:
The legal risks of conducting security research on artificial intelligence (AI) systems under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA), the United States’ primary anti-hacking statute, and other state and federal laws are not merely theoretical. Indeed, good faith security researchers and ethical hackers have been targeted by state and federal prosecutors in the past. AI companies themselves have construed carefully curated prompts as “hacking.” Indeed, countless legal threats made by companies to security researchers have been documented dating back decades. With courts increasingly scrutinizing adversarial activities like prompt injection hacking—creating new and complex legal risks—these concerns are only compounded. And today, with generative AI platforms seeing increasing use and deployment across all sectors of society, the legality of testing and evaluating these systems has taken on greater urgency.  Yet, there remains critical gaps in the literature, with little guidance for researchers as to the legality or risks of even the most common types of adversarial attacks—used by researchers and those with nefarious intentions alike. With the CFAA, there are few, if any, works on point.

This paper aims to help fill that void with an exploration of the legality of common prompt injection attacks under the CFAA.  Specifically, we analyze the legal risks for a user performing prompt injection attacks on generative AI systems. We argue, overall, that a reasonable case can be made that both direct and indirect prompt injection attacks on generative AI systems, including security testing an LLM in good faith via prompt injection, violate the CFAA. However, given uncertainties in existing case law following the United States Supreme Court’s decision in Van Buren, a recent landmark decision on the CFAA’s application, combined with uncertainties created by the fact that LLMs do not align with the types of computing systems that the CFAA originally imagined, there is room for narrower readings of the statute. As such we also explore potential legal defenses, like First Amendment arguments based on the nature of prompts, which would require more narrow judicial interpretations of the CFAA. And we offer some brief law and policy recommendations based on our findings. Although much of our focus is on users, this paper also helps defenders contextualize the types of defenses they are building to protect themselves from prompt injection.

detail.abstract: News that Brazil’s public debt will be higher than expected raises long real interest rates and weakens the real. I identify such fiscal-risk shocks in a monthly Bayesian VAR (2005–2026) by requiring survey expectations of net public debt, the 5-year real yield and the dollar to rise together. A one-standard-deviation shock raises the real yield by about 11 basis points and the dollar by 1%; the stock index falls, but imprecisely. The sharper evidence comes from 167 listed firms: one month after the shock, a firm earning all its revenue in Brazil has returned 2.5 percentage points less than one earning all its revenue abroad, and the gap persists within industries. Firms’ filings show the same divergence in revenue, and more leveraged firms pay more interest. A small open-economy model in which fiscal news works only through the premium on government debt matches these magnitudes. In the VAR, expected policy rates explain only about a fifth of the rise in the 5-year yield; the model, though not calibrated to this, gives the same split and attributes the rest to that premium.

detail.abstract: How and why do political parties form in electoral authoritarian regimes? This paper develops the concept of associational endowments: the agglomeration of local civil associations through which political organizations organize social constituencies before mass participation. Existing accounts of democratization explain when suffrage expands, institutional accounts explain how rules structure party systems, and organizational accounts show that social movements can generate durable parties. Yet, these accounts say less about why parties invest in particular forms of civil society when electoral returns are uncertain or unavailable. I argue that restricted participation makes party building asymmetric. Parliamentary opposition parties organize the included and can convert associational presence into political power. Extra-parliamentary parties organize among the excluded and therefore have stronger incentives to build social footholds through need-based institutions such as mutual aid societies, charities, credit unions, sick funds, and agricultural cooperatives. Using several originally collected and digitized datasets from the Kingdom of Hungary, I show that opposition parties' associational presence is strongly related to electoral dominance, while parliamentary incumbent associational presence is not. Moreover, the function of associations is significant for cultivating social power. Service-oriented civil society is associated with stronger extra-parliamentary dominance, yet party-affiliated service provision itself has no positive immediate electoral return. The findings show how parties can accumulate social power before democratic inclusion and why and how the organizational foundations of later mass politics are often built before democracy itself.

detail.abstract:
Ghana’s Feed Ghana Programme (2025–2028) aims to raise staple output quickly. This review examines whether a production-led strategy, without a matching expansion of postharvest capacity, risks increasing the absolute volume of food lost after harvest. It draws on peer-reviewed studies, graduate theses, national loss datasets, official budget documents and recent official statements, graded into three evidence tiers, and compares production estimates from the Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA), the United States Department of Agriculture’s Foreign Agricultural Service (USDA FAS) and the African Postharvest Losses Information System (APHLIS). Published loss estimates for Ghana range from about 12% for rice to more than 30% for yam and tomato. Estimates of 2025 maize output diverge sharply, from 3.5 million tonnes (USDA FAS) to 4.6 million tonnes (ministerial statement), which exceeds the programme's own 2025 target of 4.17 million tonnes. Usable public grain storage was reported at 40,000–50,000 tonnes in 2026. The 2025 Programme-Based Budget targets a 2.7-fold rise in tomato output by 2028 but contains no postharvest loss indicator. At published loss rates, implied annual losses at target output are 534,000–598,000 tonnes for tomato and 1.9–3.3 million tonnes for yam. USDA FAS forecasts a 16% fall in maize area for 2026/27 as prices decline under excess supply, an early sign that unabsorbed surplus weakens production incentives. Indicative costings suggest that hermetic bags and fully used warehouses avoid storage losses at about US$33–42 per tonne, against about US$122 for large steel silos. The review recommends crop-specific loss reduction targets consistent with the Malabo Declaration and SDG target 12.3, a national loss monitoring system, storage and cold-chain capacity planned against projected surplus, and wider use of proven low-cost technologies.


Keywords: postharvest losses; Feed Ghana Programme; food security; grain storage; cold chain; aflatoxin; agricultural policy; Ghana

detail.abstract: We study experimentally how retail investors process fast, high-volume order flow data under time pressure. Holding the value of information constant, a four-fold increase in message traffic reduces trading accuracy by 12%. We attribute the loss to processing costs: on fast tapes, participants report 10% higher cognitive load and commit to decisions earlier, indicating exhausted perceptual capacity. Investors nonetheless price their cognitive constraints well: they bid 11.6% less for fast tapes, and their bids match, on average, the value they extract from the data. Laboratory participants overbid by 8%, consistent with overconfidence, whereas online participants price the data almost exactly.

detail.abstract: We examine whether tax policies targeting one asset class affect other asset classes, using bonus depreciation and innovation as a setting. Bonus depreciation allows firms to accelerate tax depreciation deductions for eligible capital assets, stimulating increased capital investment. We find that this increase comes partly at the expense of investment in innovation. These declines concentrate among financially constrained firms and are economically meaningful; for every additional $1 of capital expenditure, firms reduce R&D expenditure by $0.13. The declines are greater among constrained firms in industries where capital investment responds more to bonus depreciation, consistent with bonus depreciation shifting marginal investment toward eligible capital investments. Reduced innovation investment is followed by declines in real innovation output, an unintended consequence that runs counter to the policymaker's stated growth objective. We conclude that policymakers evaluating tax policies targeting particular asset classes should consider potential spillovers to otherwise untargeted asset classes, particularly in the presence of financial constraints that can cause investment substitution.

detail.abstract: This paper starts from the numbers rather than from a theory. Using one master dataset of 15 annual observations (2011-2025) across six lenses (gender, education, formality, industry, settlement type and region), it describes what India's labour market looks like, diagnoses why, tests which economic theories survive contact with the data, and converts the surviving explanation into three implementable roadmaps. The central regularity is an inverted education gradient. In 2025 the graduate unemployment rate (UR) is 11.2% against 0.8% for the uneducated (14.0×), while 89.2% of the workforce remains unorganised and graduate formal absorption has slipped from 8.5% to 6.9%. The graduate labour force grew ×2.46 (27.0 → 66.5 Mn) against ×1.32 for the total workforce, and an indicative 80.1% of net new employment since 2011 is unorganised. Women graduates carry the heaviest burden (peak 26.3% in 2017; 15.0% in 2025), youth unemployment runs at roughly three times the all-India rate throughout the PLFS era, and urban unemployment has run at about twice the rural rate since 2020. The pattern fits a segmented, queue-based structural model (structural unemployment, matching frictions, wait unemployment and dual-sector segmentation) and contradicts the unemployment corollary of pure human-capital theory. We propose (i) a formalisation strategy built around the first formal job, (ii) an education-industry alignment programme built on district skill mapping and apprenticeship-embedded degrees, and (iii) a corridor-based regional job-creation strategy that begins by repairing the measurement of regional unemployment. Because most series in the master dataset are modelled estimates, every finding is graded by evidence quality and should be treated as hypothesis-grade until replaced by unit-level PLFS tables.

detail.abstract: Public debt bubbles can migrate when sovereigns compete for savings. In a two-country overlapping-generations model, foreign safe-debt issuance draws savings away from domestic debt, increasing domestic fiscal risk. If the recovery rate on defaulted domestic bonds is low enough, sufficiently large foreign issuance eliminates the domestic full-repayment stationary equilibrium. Across this equilibrium shift, debt demand moves discontinuously toward the foreign safe issuer. The foreign interest rate falls despite increased issuance, whereas domestic debt valuation contracts. This sovereign bubble flight expands the foreign government's capacity to finance spending through debt rollover.

detail.abstract: This study examined the macroeconomic determinants of education recurrent expenditure in Nigeria from 1999 to 2023 using the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) approach. Annual time series data were sourced from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) Statistical Bulletin, while the study adopted an ex-post facto research design. The Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) unit root test revealed mixed integration orders of I(0) and I(1), thereby justifying the use of the ARDL technique. The ARDL Bounds Test established the existence of a weak long-run relationship among the variables, while the Error Correction Model (ECM) revealed a negative and statistically significant adjustment coefficient of-1.024624, indicating a rapid speed of adjustment with slight overshooting (>100%) towards long-run equilibrium. The findings showed that Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and inflation rate exerted negative and statistically significant influences on education recurrent expenditure, whereas non-oil revenue exerted a positive and statistically significant influence. Recession shocks exerted a positive but statistically insignificant influence during the study period. Diagnostic tests confirmed that the estimated model was statistically reliable and free from serial correlation and heteroskedasticity problems. Although the CUSUM test revealed slight structural instability in the later years of the study period, likely associated with recessionary and post-COVID macroeconomic disturbances, the CUSUMSQ test confirmed that the variance structure of the model remained stable. The study concluded that macroeconomic conditions significantly influence education recurrent expenditure in Nigeria and recommended improved macroeconomic stability, inflation control, and enhanced non-oil revenue generation to sustain educational financing.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a no-arbitrage implied volatility surface forecasting framework based on conditional diffusion models comparing U-Net and Transformer backbone architectures. The approach combines historical SPX options data with synthetic SABR and Heston-COS volatility surfaces and incorporates arbitrage and smoothness constraints during training. While a postprocessing repair step enforces financial consistency in generated forecasts. Empirical results show that diffusion models produce stable and realistic volatility surface forecasts and capture key market features such as smile skew and term-structure dynamics. The Transformer architecture achieves comparable training loss with substantially fewer parameters, the U-Net delivers superior out-of-sample forecasting accuracy across moneyness regions as well being computationally cheaper. Training-time arbitrage penalties do not eliminate arbitrage violations and, in some cases, reduce predictive performance, whereas a pure diffusion objective combined with post-hoc surface repair yields the best results. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of diffusion-based methods for probabilistic volatility surface forecasting and highlight the limitations of model architecture, loss design, and post-processing in achieving financially consistent forecasts.

detail.abstract: Physical cash settles finally, privately at small value, and without fees or private credit risk, but only face to face. Banking overcame distance by turning money into a claim on an intermediary, and today's tokenization into wholesale central bank digital currency (CBDC), tokenized deposits, and stablecoins changes the technology while preserving that structure. This paper asks whether digital money can behave like cash at a distance. Using cash as a normative benchmark, a comparative institutional analysis of five regimes across nine dimensions finds that, beyond three dimensions that exclude intermediaries by definition, privacy and offline capability, though technically feasible, are limited by intermediaries' legal obligations. The paper then specifies "Perfect Digital Cash," a sovereign-issued, hardware-enforced bearer instrument, separating the primitives that exist from those that do not, the hardest being a decentralized point-to-point network. If built, it would meet the cash benchmark on every property except universal access while adding reach over distance. Compliance would rest on statutory thresholds instead of surveillance, and issuance as well as protocol parameters would be rule-bound, so removing intermediaries relocates state authority over money instead of eroding it. A stylized model shows that policy reaches holders only through the opportunity cost of holding, that the effective lower bound rises to about zero, and that deposit markets become contestable, most when rates are low. The issuer's asset policy governs the banking consequences, including deposit-franchise compression, pressure on credit to small firms, and a transitional rise in run risk, after which deposit-based run risk falls while aggregate run risk depends on where maturity transformation migrates. Technical, regulatory, and political barriers remain, and the result is a design specification for a research program, not a deployment proposal.

detail.abstract: We examine how digital attention relates to retail investors' portfolio choices and investment performance. Using a unique dataset form Ant Fund, we measure investors' digital attention by their monthly reading time on the platform and link it to their actual performance. Greater digital attention predicts lower subsequent portfolio returns, and this pattern holds for over six months. Riskier asset allocation and excessive trading may further amplify this negative relationship. We also highlight the role of usergenerated content (UGC), showing that both greater exposure to UGC and active information selection through subscriptions and likes are associated with more pronounced underperformance among attentive investors. These findings highlight how the information environment shaped by social interactions influences the relationship between digital attention and investment performance.

detail.abstract: Temporary labour-migration regimes can incorporate workers deeply into production while limiting pathways to membership. This article develops recognition-stratified incorporation to explain the mismatch between economic and administrative inclusion and social and political standing. Qualitative documentary, policy and media analysis of 128 public items examines Singapore during COVID-19, principally 2020-2021. Five linked mechanisms organise the interpretation: legal temporariness, spatial separation, risk-centred visibility, mediated voice and labour disposability. The materials examined foreground migrant workers as essential labour, administratively legible populations and epidemiological subjects, while revealing constraints on autonomous claims-making and prospective membership. Communicative misrecognition is proposed as the link through which legal and material arrangements acquire unequal public meaning. The analysis interprets a recurring configuration rather than estimating frame prevalence or identifying causal effects. Pandemic governance made pre-existing dependencies visible, while care and participatory communication complicated any account of uniformly absent recognition. The framework distinguishes economic, administrative, social and political incorporation and proposes scope conditions involving employer-dependent temporary status, restricted mobility, segregated accommodation and weak collective representation. It offers a basis for comparative investigation of integration without membership.

detail.abstract: This study examines whether mandatory disclosure of derivatives and hedging activities affects private debt contracting when lenders already possess private information about borrowers. Exploiting the adoption of SFAS 161, which mandates structured and disaggregated disclosures on derivative and hedging activities, we find that firms that increase their derivatives and hedging disclosures experience loan spreads that are 9.6 basis points lower than those of firms with little disclosure change. Cross-sectional evidence is consistent with improved comparability as the main mechanism for the effect. We also find that the reduction in loan spreads is larger for firms with more extensive pre-adoption disclosures, consistent with standardized reporting rather than new information driving the effect. Loan spreads also decline when industry peers increase disclosure, suggesting benchmarking externalities from comparable reporting. The effects are also stronger for firms with greater agency frictions, where voluntary disclosure is less reliable, and in syndicated and non-relationship loans, where borrower-specific private information is less informative. Additional analysis shows that pricing effects are concentrated in newly originated loans, whereas for existing loans, lenders relax covenant restrictiveness. Overall, our study shows that mandatory disclosure improves the comparability of complex financial information and influences debt contracting even in settings where lenders have access to private information.

title: An Empirical Framework for Changing Marital Matching Patterns

detail.title: An Empirical Framework for Changing Marital Matching Patterns

detail.abstract: Recent U.S. marital matching exhibits three known facts: (i) marriage has declined while cohabitation has risen at every education level; (ii) both unions have become more stable; and (iii) union formation passes through two regimes dividing at 2008-substitution from marriage toward cohabitation, then a retreat from partnership altogether. Static models of marriage matching, such as that of Choo and Siow (2006), explain the decline of marriage as a fall in the gains to marriage. But a fall in the gains to marriage cannot explain the concurrent increase in the duration of marriages. To fit the data, this paper estimates time-varying match values together with match-formation and dissolution costs for different marital matches. The retreat from marriage operates through entry. Marriage-formation costs rose past marriage gains that were themselves rising, most sharply for the less-educated, while stability rose because unions became more valuable, not harder to leave. Cohabitation's rise is mostly its own market with higher value, greater durability, and a costlier upgrade to marriage. I use the estimates to test a number of explanations for these changes. I find that only men's declining labour-force attachment robustly moves the net gain to forming a match, and the bulk of the transition remains unexplained.

title: Delayed or Declining? Marriage and Fertility in the U.S

detail.abstract: Since 2008, U.S. birth rates have fallen nearly twice as fast as fertility intentions. Is the shortfall delay, marriage postponed so that fewer childbearing years are spent where births are most likely, or decline, fewer births at a given age whether married or not? I estimate a dynamic marriage matching model with endogenous divorce and fertility on U.S. survey data for 2008-2023, then hold each estimated component at its 2008 value in turn, resolving the marriage market and retracing the fertility decisions that follow. Of the fall the model explains, a third is delay and two thirds decline. The delay comes from the cost of forming a marriage, which rose faster than the payoff to a match. The decline lies outside marriage, where the net gain to a birth fell; within marriage there is little to explain. Both movements are concentrated among adults under thirty.

detail.abstract: I study the role of the world interest rate level and volatility in the duration of sovereign defaults. Across 93 countries over 200 years, I find that default duration is strongly and positively associated with the expected volatility of the world interest rate. A one-percentage-point increase in expected volatility is associated with an increase in median default duration from 6.3 to 13.1 years. More politically polarized countries remain in default for longer, and this relationship is stronger when the debt burden is larger. To rationalize these findings, I develop a model in which a country in default holds a real option to settle with a representative creditor. The world interest rate is the only source of uncertainty. Settlement restores the country's access to international capital markets and reestablishes a deterministic output flow. However, settlement comes at an irreversible political cost, determined by distributional conflict. I show that higher expected volatility in the world interest rate increases the option value of waiting and, when the political cost of settlement is sufficiently low, the expected duration of default. Structural estimation of the model suggests that the political cost of settlement is approximately 5 percent of yearly real GDP.

All participants provided informed consent before taking part, and the research was conducted in accordance with the ethical standards of the approving board and the principles of the Declaration of Helsinki.

detail.abstract: Social desirability bias (SDB) and demand characteristics (DC) are two classic issues in experimental social science. SDB refers to the deeply ingrained tendency for individuals to present themselves in an overly positive light, and DC refers to participants' tendency to respond the way they believe the researcher desires. Researchers have sought to address these issues in a variety of ways, such as concealing the purpose of the research, explicitly encouraging participants to respond honestly and authentically, and measuring participants' response tendencies and accounting for them in statistical analysis. Despite the long history of attention to these issues, foundational research on these topics occurred long before the advent of online participant panels and the resultant transition to online, anonymous research. This shift raises questions regarding the state of these issues in research today and what steps researchers can take to mitigate them. We conducted two pre-registered studies with online panel participants (total N = 2827) that were designed to enhance or reduce SDB and DC, respectively, based on the extant literature on both topics. In both studies, none of the manipulated features consistently affected SDB or DC. These findings contribute to the understanding of two classic experimental effects in online, anonymous research and raise questions about the relevance of both issues to research today. Alongside such drastic changes in how research is conducted, researchers may need to reconsider core issues from the history of the field and focus instead on emergent threats to data quality triggered by novel aspects of today's research settings.

detail.abstract: The present study evaluates a dual-momentum strategy that combines relative-momentum selection between a semiconductor ETF (SMH) and a utilities ETF (XLU) with an absolute-momentum filter referencing a cash proxy (BIL) and a safe-haven asset (GLD). Using monthly price data spanning May 2007 to July 2026 (231 observations), the strategy is back-tested against a buy-and-hold benchmark (SMH), a 50/50 SMH-XLU mix, and a pure relative-momentum rule. Performance metrics—including compound annual growth rate (CAGR), Sharpe and Sortino ratios, maximum drawdown, and drawdown duration—are computed after accounting for a 10 bps transaction cost per switch. Sensitivity analyses examine the impact of transaction-cost levels (0–25 bps) and look-back windows (6, 9, 12 months). A GARCH(1,1) model is fitted to the dual-momentum return series to assess volatility persistence and to generate short-term volatility forecasts. Results confirm the hypothesis that dual momentum sacrifices a modest amount of upside (≈115 bps yr⁻¹) to achieve markedly lower drawdowns (-22.5 % vs. -44.5 % for the benchmark) and superior risk-adjusted scores (Sharpe 0.93 vs. 0.85). The strategy’s edge remains robust across transaction-cost variations and is strongest at the 12-month look-back, and the estimated GARCH parameters indicate a highly persistent yet mean-reverting volatility process (α = 0.057, β = 0.938, α+β = 0.995). The findings suggest that dual momentum delivers a smoother equity curve without relying heavily on gold, instead allocating to utilities during market stress.

detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of data centers (DCs), driven largely by artificial intelligence, creates substantial new electricity demand, may lead to congestion in power networks and pressure on increasing electricity prices. Knowledge of DC operation is largely limited to operators, and DCs are often characterized by their rated capacity rather than actual consumption, so their real impact on power systems remains unclear. This review provides background on DC operations and reviews literature on DC flexibility in power systems and electricity markets. The levers examined include temporal and spatial shifting of computing loads, cooling, renewable integration, sector integration such as waste heat use in district heating, and energy storage. These levers can reduce DC operating costs while benefiting the grid and markets. However, reported benefits depend strongly on the share of deferrable workloads, which is often assumed rather than measured, and on electricity market design. Participation may further be limited by quality of service requirements and data protection laws restricting crossborder data transfers. DCs are found to have significant flexibility potential, but as they differ widely in type and context, no single solution applies to all. Policy recommendations are proposed for integrating DCs into the power system.

detail.abstract: American housing policy has failed not through neglect but through capture. The Low-Income Housing Tax Credit, the federal government’s primary affordable housing tool, channels approximately $15 billion annually through a transaction structure that consumes the majority of its value before it reaches housing construction. This paper argues that the LIHTC program exemplifies captocracy — the systematic capture of public policy mechanisms by financial interests — and that regulatory reform alone cannot correct a structural problem embedded in the program’s design. Direct public investment, not additional market complexity, is the necessary response. The pattern mirrors precedents in banking, energy, and telecommunications, where industry capture of subsidy mechanisms produces structural inefficiency resistant to conventional reform.

detail.abstract: Risk-taking is an important driver for regional development. If rural populations are more risk-averse than their urban counterparts, this may present a challenge for achieving balanced regional growth, which is an important political objective. This paper investigates whether a rural-urban divide in risk preferences exists and, if so, whether it is contextual or compositional. Using a representative survey of the Norwegian population, I elicit risk preferences through an income lottery method and classify individuals by levels of risk aversion. Regression results show that rural residents are indeed more riskaverse on average, and that the difference is driven by lower risk aversion in the capital area. However, a mediation analysis indicates that this difference may be explained by compositional demographic factors, namely age and education, rather than the rural or urban context itself. The analysis also confirms associations between risk aversion and gender, age, and education, aligning with previous literature.

detail.abstract:
Philippine labor laws, inluenced by patriarchal structures, have historically marginalized women and queers. This paper examines the intersection of gender, sexuality, and labor rights, highlighting the ongoing challenges faced by the queer community in the workplace, particularly regarding leave beneits. The study delves into the impact of patriarchal norms on employee compensation rights, leave beneits, and social security provisions. It explores how legal frameworks, such as the Magna Carta for Women, the Solo Parent Leave Act, the Violence Against Women and Children Act, and relevant jurisprudences have attempted to address gender-based disparities but often fall short in protecting the queer community.

This study examines the intersecting institutions and their respective policies using a conceptual-legal framework grounded in the leading legal philosophies, feminist legal theory, and queer intersectionality to analyze the patriarchal and heteronormative biases embedded in Philippine labor laws, especially those governing employee leave rights. As a practical output, the economic and non-economic provisions of Collective Bargaining Agreements (CBAs) and their role in ensuring fair employee compensation, welfare, and workplace equity are also explored as an alternative solution. It further explores how corporate social responsibility (CSR), corporate governance, and company practices—particularly those extending inclusive beneits to queer employees—interact with labor law principles such as Article 100 of the Labor Code.

To reconcile the jurisprudential and statutory inconsistencies identified in this study, a more comprehensive but concrete legislative and policy framework is recommended—one that critically reexamines the legal deinition of gender and the scope of employee beneits. The paper concludes by advancing policy and doctrinal reforms aimed at dismantling patriarchal structures embedded within labor legislation, thereby fostering a more inclusive, equitable, and gender-responsive labor landscape in the Philippines.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether top-of-book depth imbalance predicts short-term market quality beyond trade-based order imbalance, and whether the relationship varies with participant identity. Using 17 billion order messages for 99 NSE-listed stocks in May 2024, we regress lagged depth imbalance (DI) on quoted spread, effective spread, and undercutting frequency. A one-standard-deviation increase in DI narrows quoted spreads by 0.146 basis points; the same shock to trade-based order imbalance widens spreads-12 times smaller in absolute magnitude-exposing trade imbalance as a directionally misleading proxy. Decomposing DI by participant type reveals opposing effects: HFT depth imbalance narrows quoted spreads by 0.295 basis points and suppresses undercutting by 89.9 events per minute, consistent with committed liquidity provision that crowds out competitive order placement. AAT depth imbalance widens quoted spreads by 0.248 basis points and amplifies undercutting by 63.2 events per minute, reflecting a pre-execution adverse selection response three times larger than the equivalent tradebased signal. Cross-sectional tests show both effects intensify sharply in high-algorithmic environments-HFT depth imbalance suppresses an additional 192 undercutting events per minute while AAT depth imbalance widens spreads by an additional 0.041 basis points in highalgo, large-cap stocks. The findings have direct implications for market surveillance and institutional execution strategy.

detail.abstract:
Dealer gamma exposure (GEX) is widely used by practitioners as a gauge of intraday
fragility, but its causal footprint on volatility and liquidity in the NASDAQ-100 is not
established. This paper develops a hedging-feedback model in which net dealer gamma,
scaled by market depth, sets the autocorrelation structure of intraday returns, and
derives closed-form expressions for the volatility multiplier, the last-30-minute
momentum coefficient and a fragility threshold. It then tests the model's comparative
statics in a book-level Monte Carlo (2,000 sessions, 5-minute bars, Black–Scholes delta
hedging of a strike-by-expiry dealer book, square-root price impact and leveraged-ETF
rebalancing). Common random numbers measure every effect against an identical no-
hedging counterfactual. In the illustrative calibration, net GEX of −$6 bn per 1% move
raises daily return volatility by 7.9% under continuous hedging and by 12.2% when
hedging is concentrated near the close, lifts the probability of a >3% intraday range from
9.6% (zero net GEX) to 13.7%, and yields a last-30-minute momentum coefficient of +0.14
(+$6 bn gives −0.13). Leveraged-ETF rebalancing adds a sign-independent momentum
term that is sub-additive with dealer flow. Five-minute realized volatility rises under both
signs of GEX, a microstructure artifact of temporary impact, while the execution-cost
proxy moves by under 3%. The paper closes with a specification for estimating these
effects on NDX, QQQ and NQ data. No empirical estimates are reported.

detail.abstract: Agriculture is central to livelihoods in East Africa, employing nearly 60% of the labor force, yet productivity growth has remained modest. This study examines the determinants of agricultural productivity in Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda, and Rwanda between 2000 and 2023. Using panel data from the World Development Indicators and a fixed-effects regression framework, agricultural value added per worker is modeled as a function of fertilizer consumption, arable land use, rural population share, and GDP growth. Diagnostic tests confirmed no multicollinearity, while heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation were detected and corrected with clustered standard errors. Panel unit root tests revealed mixed integration orders, with fertilizer consumption stationary after first differencing. Robustness checks, including specifications with lagged fertilizer consumption, robust standard errors, and random effects, demonstrated coefficient stability, and residual cross-section dependence tests indicated independence across countries. Results show that fertilizer consumption (β = 0.1085, p < 0.01), arable land use (β = 0.7648, p < 0.01), and rural population share (β = 1.4112, p < 0.01) significantly enhance productivity, while GDP growth is statistically insignificant (β = 0.0013, p > 0.05). These findings suggest that productivity improvements in East Africa are driven primarily by input intensification and labor utilization rather than macroeconomic expansion. The study concludes that policies expanding fertilizer access, promoting sustainable land management, and enhancing rural labor efficiency are essential to support agricultural transformation and strengthen food security.

detail.abstract: Rising interest rates squeeze real estate cash flows, and capital expenditures (capex) are the line item most likely to be cut. This paper, written in 2017 as the Federal Reserve began raising rates, argues that capex cuts, through deferred maintenance or lower-quality repairs, lead to more property and liability claims, higher insurance premiums, lower net operating income (NOI), and, over time, weaker valuations. Drawing on interviews with senior executives at two of Philadelphia's largest REITs, an insurance practice leader, and a Columbia real estate professor, it proposes a two-part response: protect capex budgets internally, and strengthen representation in the insurance market externally. It sets out the implications for five groups: property managers, current owners, new buyers, publicmarket investors, and insurers. A 2026 epilogue revisits the thesis after the 2022-23 rate hikes and the commercial property insurance hard market that followed. Reviewing Federal Reserve research on financial pressure and maintenance, insurer data on building condition and loss costs, and current underwriting practice, it finds that the evidence since 2017 largely supports the original thesis, and it refines one prediction about relative returns.

detail.abstract: Organized crime is spreading, and little is known about how to fight it. What happens to crime when the state dismantles the territorial base of a criminal organization? I study the 2016 takeover of The Bronx, the Bogotá enclave that housed Colombia's largest open-air drug market. Recorded violent crime in the enclave fell about 70% in three months, an effect that faded after 18 months. Qualitative records show where the market went, and recorded crime did not detectably rise there or within 5 km. The takeover passes a cost-benefit test at costs below US$3 to 6 million.

detail.abstract: This paper examines agency problems in Ecuadorian corporate law considering the 2020 and 2023 amendments to the Companies Act (Ley de Compañías). It argues that corporate law serves two functions: removing barriers and preventing and resolving corporate conflicts. Drawing on Kraakman et al., it identifies three agency problems: between shareholders and managers, among shareholders, and between the company and its stakeholders. It contends that the main conflict in Ecuador is between controlling and minority shareholders. This is because ownership is concentrated in families and business groups and the securities market is very small. The paper reviews the ex ante and ex post remedies the amendments introduced: approval of related-party transactions by disinterested shareholders, the corporate liability action, the derivative action, the minority oppression action and the business judgment rule. It concludes that in concentrated-ownership systems the duty of loyalty matters more than the duty of care, and that fiduciary duties must constrain the controlling shareholder.
